bib.title: GPT3Mix: Leveraging Large-scale Language Models for Text Augmentation
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2021

question: Can prompting a large language model with a mixture of real examples generate realistic, soft-labelled synthetic text that improves small fine-tuned classifiers in low-data settings?
hypothesis: Prompt-based mix of k real examples plus LM-predicted soft labels yields better augmentation than shallow or latent-space mixing methods, and the gain is not just memorization.
contributions: Prompt-based data augmentation with large LMs on top of PLM fine-tuning
GPT3Mix: simple text augmentation eliciting LM knowledge
Analysis of the mechanism behind prompt-powered augmentation
RT20: new movie-review benchmark post-dating GPT-3 data, to rule out memorization

method.summary: Sample k=2 labelled examples, build a prompt (description header, text-label pairs, prefix), let GPT-3 generate a new text and its label token; the normalized label-token likelihoods give a soft label. Synthetic samples (ratio 10 to real) are added to the real subsample and a BERT/DistilBERT classifier is fine-tuned with cross-entropy.
method.task: low-resource text classification via LM-generated data augmentation with soft-label distillation

datasets.name: SST-2
datasets.split: sub-sampled 0.1%, 0.3%, 1.0% class-balanced training set; full set in one experiment

datasets.name: RT20
datasets.size: 1,100 positive and 1,100 negative reviews for 62 movies
datasets.source: Rotten Tomatoes critic reviews of movies released 2020 or later; crawled
datasets.preprocessing: lowercased; spaces added around certain special characters

models.name: GPT-3 davinci (generator, default)
models.params: inferred: 175B (footnote 7 lists known sizes 2.7B, 6.7B, 13B, 175B for ada, babbage, curie, davinci; not officially disclosed)
models.architecture: autoregressive LM via OpenAI API Beta

other.ablation generators: ada, babbage, curie, davinci; GPT-2 large 774M; GPT-neo 1.3B

models.name: BERT-base
models.architecture: transformer encoder + two fully connected classifier layers

training.objective: cross-entropy on real samples (hard labels) plus synthetic samples with soft pseudo-labels
training.epochs: early stopping on validation score, patience 20 epochs
training.seeds: 15 data seeds per Sec 4.1; Table 1 caption says repeated 10 times

other.augmentation ratio: 10 synthetic per real by default; 5 in Tables 4,7; 3 in Table 8; 1:1 on full SST-2

inference.samples: augmentation ratio 10 synthetic samples per real sample (default)
inference.prompting: k=2 randomly chosen (uniform) real examples in a template of description header, text-label pairs, prefix; label generated after text; avg ~300 tokens (prompt + generation) per augmentation

parameters.soft label: p(y'|x') proportional to p_LM(v(y') | P(x',S_T)), label-token likelihoods normalized
parameters.task spec: S=(text type T, label type L, verbalizer v); chosen per task on validation, Table 9

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: classification accuracy on test set, mean+-std over repeated trials

eval.protocol: class-balanced subsamples at 15 seeds (text) vs 10 repeats (Table 1 caption); mean+-std; early stopping on validation

prompts.text:
Each item in the following list contains a <text type> and the respective <label type>. <label type> is one of '<label token 1>', ..., or '<label token N>'.
<text type>: <example text 1> (<label type>: <example label 1>)
...
<text type>: <example text k> (<label type>: <example label k>)
<text type>:

evidence.quote: top-p and the temperature was set to 1 and the frequency penalty was set to 0.02

results.claim: GPT3Mix lifts BERT-base average accuracy at 0.1% data across 7 tasks.
results.note: Text says improves baseline 'as much as 18.6%'; table difference is 10.8 points (about 18.5% relative)
results.table: Table 1, row Average 0.1%, BERT-base Ours 69.2 vs none 58.4

results.claim: On SST-2 0.1% GPT3Mix gives large gain over EDA and back-translation.
results.table: Table 1, row SST-2 0.1%, BERT-base Ours 78.0 vs none 57.1

results.claim: BERT-large with GPT3Mix on 1.0% SST-2 matches BERT-base on full data.
results.table: Table 2, row 1.0%, column Ours 90.8 vs none 87.8

results.claim: RT20 (post-GPT-3 data) still shows large gains, ruling out memorization as sole cause.
results.table: Table 1, RT20 1.0% DistilBERT Ours 72.3 vs none 56.2

results.claim: Soft labels beat hard labels from beam search.
results.table: Table 7, row 0.1%, Soft-labels 71.2 vs Hard Labels 61.6

results.note: k=4 gives 74.6 at 0.1% but k=2 chosen for cost

results.claim: Larger generator is better: davinci vs ada.
Open-source GPT-neo 1.3B gives gains close to davinci.
Task-specific spec beats generic spec on SST-2.
Full SST-2 with 1:1 synthetic raises BERT-base accuracy.
results.quote: the accuracy of BERTbase from 90.33% to 93.25% (2.92% improvement)

results.claim: A wrong label-type word (linguistic acceptability) collapses COLA 0.1% augmentation.

limits: Handcrafted task specifications chosen on validation per task; poor spec can drop below baseline (COLA 38.8%).
Only classification with single-token labels; GPT-3 inference cost grows with k.
On TREC6 and SUBJ 1% GPT3Mix does not beat baselines (Table 1); label vagueness on SUBJ.
Possible propagation of LM bias and toxicity (Ethical Considerations).
Inconsistent seed count: 15 data seeds in Sec 4.1 vs repeated 10 times in Table 1 caption; no per-dataset sizes given; ablations use curie/DistilBERT and lower ratios.
GPT-3 davinci via OpenAI Beta API has since been retired.

terms.definition: generating synthetic text from a mixture of real in-context examples with an LM, labelled by LM soft-labels
S=(T,L,v): text type, label type, label-token verbalizer

lineage.work: Distilling the knowledge in a neural network
SST-2, CR, COLA, TREC6, MPQA, SUBJ
